headline: First quarter after the Versace sale: revenue -4%, MK Americas -9%; adjusted EPS $0.81 tops estimates, but shares fell ~10%.
guidance_note: Reuters described a forecast bump; FY26 revenue ~ $3.45-3.475B. Prior range not confirmed.
key_messages: Michael Kors revenue -5.6% (-7.3% cc) to $858M; Americas -9% on inventory clearing, lower daigou and less off-price selling.
Full-price sales improved sequentially with higher AUR and gross margin as promotions were cut.
MK operating margin fell to 13.9% from 16.2%.
Versace sale to Prada completed; net debt fell to ~$80M at quarter end per one summary.

consumer.big_ticket: Holiday MK demand down in the Americas; full-price selling improved while markdown sales fell.
consumer.pricing: Higher AUR from less promotional activity.

macro_read: Over the 2025 holidays, MK shoppers bought less once discounts were reduced, a sign that this aspirational customer is price sensitive.
notes: Growth is as reported; Capri gives no constant-currency figure for the Americas. Versace was sold to Prada in December 2025; Jimmy Choo is still part of Capri.
Versace sale to Prada closed in Dec 2025, and Versace is reported as a discontinued operation; Jimmy Choo stays in continuing operations.
Reuters said shares fell 10% on the day; final close not confirmed, so null.
Consensus figures (EPS $0.78, revenue ~$1.00B) are from MarketBeat only. GAAP EPS $0.47 vs adjusted $0.81.
Americas decline: the transcript says MK Americas -9%; another summary cites a 7% Americas retail decline (different measure).
